animation.description: The 3 source renders are near-duplicate poses of the same truck (not a real sweep/angle sequence) -- cycle slowly between them for a subtle idle "settle" rather than claiming a dramatic aim animation.

source: User-provided FIBERNET bucket-truck sheet (JPG, checkerboard background). Used the 3 large row-1 renders only; rows 2-4 (16 smaller variants) left unused.
cleanup: Background removed via border flood-fill through grayscale pixels only.

Despeckle kept every connected component >=60px (not a single "largest blob"), so the boom-to-body connector was never at risk of being dropped -- verified all 3 frames keep the full truck+arm intact.

No per-frame rescaling applied: all 3 source renders are already the same real-world scale (verified visually), so resizing was skipped to avoid introducing distortion from unreliable auto-measurement.
Alignment anchors the sprite's rear-bumper edge (rightmost opaque pixel) to a fixed tile x, and the wheel-contact point (lowest opaque pixel) to a fixed tile y, in every frame.
notes: Turret/structure sprite for the Bucket-Truck Boss signature + deployable -- static vehicle art, no walk cycle.

Honest limitation: the 3 renders are compositional variations, not a hand-drawn boom-sweep animation, so do not market this as a dynamic aim/tracking animation -- it is a mild idle cycle for visual life.
